identity_evidence.identity_notes: Current AFD-derived cached taxonomy treats Manorina melanocephala leachi as an accepted subspecies within M. melanocephala, not a separate species. The existing historical-name bridge and original diagnostics therefore establish species identity, while the Tasmanian origin prevents describing this as a verified Sydney nominate form. The former hold combines a valid regional limitation with an unnecessarily strict requirement for species-level use. Accepting this historical representation does not assert that Tasmanian leachi is the local breeding form or a Sydney visitor. Retain a plain Tasmanian-form label. If the library later promises subspecies-accurate local plumage, use a separately verified mainland alternative then.

Gould Myzantha garrula cites Merops garrulus Latham, Index Ornithologicus supplement, and explicitly distinguishes other miners of northern/western Australia. AFD nominate profile lists Merops garrulus Latham1801. The historical printed page is xxiv while AFD gives34; this discrepancy is retained. The image, detailed diagnosis and eastern distribution independently support species identity.

Historical illustration of the Tasmanian form of Noisy Miner; the species also occurs in Sydney. Gould states the pictured specimens came from Van Diemens Land. This does not claim Tasmanian leachi is a Sydney breeding form or visitor.

identity_evidence.identity_notes: Gould IV/55 is the mainland red-wattled species. Its own account explicitly separates it from the Tasmanian IV/54 inauris, and describes short blood-red wattles, silvery cheeks, yellow belly and white tail tips. KU MODS for the exact published IV/55 explicitly identifies Anthochaera carunculata (Shaw1790), current Red Wattlebird; current AFD profile and BirdLife diagnostics agree. Do not transfer this mapping to older Synopsis or Vigors/Horsfield carunculata usages, which Gould explicitly warns were misapplied to the Tasmanian bird.
Red neck wattle, pale cheek, streaked grey-brown body, yellow belly and pale tail tips agree. Several outer tail tips run into the right scan edge; do not invent missing tips.
Mainland Red Wattlebird identity supported; original account excludes Tasmania and discusses NSW/Upper Hunter observations. Exact illustrated specimen locality unspecified.
